title: Two score choices and three peak-separation rules miss Kepler-90 i with a two-day trend window
abstract: We audit a failed search control for the known planet Kepler-90 i. The original period grid and scores repeat exactly at all 175,531 points. With a two-day trend window, the best grid point within 0.1 percent of the known period ranks 4,454th for the likelihood score and 4,496th for the depth signal-to-noise score. Neither score selects that period in its first 20 choices at any of three peak-separation settings. Thus a smaller peak separation alone does not fix this failure. A separate half-day trend test gives grid rank 1650. These tests use fourteen Kepler release 25 files and a fixed early/later time split. We do not find a new planet, calibrate search completeness, or identify the cause of other peaks. The package includes code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes, and repeat steps. External source data stay outside the package.

display.caption: Early search scores near planet i and box depths at its supplied orbit. Score curves use their own global maxima. Later data use the same telescope.
